item.subject: Advanced Mathematics
item.stem:
In the ΔABC the altitudes BN and CM intersect at point S. The measure of ∠MSB is 40° and the measure of ∠SBC is 20°. Write a PROOF of the following statement:

“ΔABC is isosceles.”

Give geometric reasons for statements in your proof.

[Image: Triangle ABC with altitudes BN and CM intersecting at S]

descriptors:
Correct proof. Proves that ∠B = ∠C using the following facts:

• the sum of angles in any triangle is 180°.
• if two angles of a triangle are equal, the triangle is isosceles.
and possibly also uses:
• vertically opposite angles are equal.
• supplementary angles add to 180°.
The concept of congruence is not used.
As code 20 but somewhere in the proof uses the fact that some triangles: e.g. triangles BCM and CBN, OR triangles BMS and CNS, are congruent.
All other fully correct and complete proofs.
As in codes 20-21 shows ∠B and ∠C are equal giving steps in logical order, but omits one step or one reason or gives one incorrect reason.
As in codes 20-21 shows ∠B and ∠C are equal, states correct geometric facts but not in a logically correct order.
Shows measures of angles correctly on figure but no geometric facts mentioned or argumentation given.
Incorrect argumentation and/or includes more than one incorrect geometric fact, step, or reason.
"Proof" is circular; makes use of statements which are equivalent to what is to be proven.
Crossed-out, illegible, or impossible to interpret.

item.scoring_notes: Note: To be considered correct, all responses must include mention of all geometric facts used, all calculations made, and a conclusion
item.figure_description: A triangle ABC with vertex A at the top, vertex B at the bottom left, and vertex C at the bottom right. Segment BN is an altitude drawn from B to AC, with a right-angle symbol at N. Segment CM is an altitude drawn from C to AB, with a right-angle symbol at M. BN and CM intersect at interior point S. The angle MSB is marked with an arc and labeled 40°. The angle SBC is marked with an arc and labeled 20°.

slope.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 2-point item with the generalized partial credit model (GPCM), which TIMSS uses for constructed-response items worth 2 or 3 points, in the calibration "Concurrent scaling of the TIMSS Advanced 1995 and 2008 advanced mathematics data". What is the item's slope (discrimination) parameter a? A higher a means that the item separates students of lower and higher mathematics ability more sharply. Choose the value closest to it.

location.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 2-point item with the generalized partial credit model (GPCM), which TIMSS uses for constructed-response items worth 2 or 3 points, in the calibration "Concurrent scaling of the TIMSS Advanced 1995 and 2008 advanced mathematics data". What is the item's location (difficulty) parameter b? b is on a logit scale on which the students of the calibration average about 0; a higher b means a harder item. Choose the value closest to it.

step1.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 2-point item with the generalized partial credit model (GPCM), which TIMSS uses for constructed-response items worth 2 or 3 points, in the calibration "Concurrent scaling of the TIMSS Advanced 1995 and 2008 advanced mathematics data". What is the item's step 1 parameter d1? In the GPCM, b - d1 is the ability at which earning the first point becomes more likely than earning no point, so a higher d1 means that this point is earned at a lower ability; the steps sum to 0. Choose the value closest to it.
